clean_source_blocks.text: The current outbreak of Ebola in the DRC and Uganda began in May A trial of potential treatments for the strain of virus behind the current deadly Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) has begun, the World Health Organization (WHO) has announced. The first patient has been enrolled in the DRC, WHO chief Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus said on Thursday. More than 1,400 cases and 438 deaths have been confirmed in the DRC alone, according to the WHO. There are currently no approved vaccines or treatments for the Bundibugyo virus strain of the disease, which is highly infectious. The current trial is sponsored by the WHO, and is being co-ordinated by scientists at the Institut National de Recherche Biomédicale in DRC, the Institute of Tropical Medicine in Belgium, and the University of Oxford in the UK.

The current trial is sponsored by the WHO, and is being co-ordinated by scientists at the Institut National de Recherche Biomédicale in DRC, the Institute of Tropical Medicine in Belgium, and the University of Oxford in the UK.

Speaking to reporters from the WHO headquarters in Geneva on Thursday, Tedros said: "The clinical trial of two therapeutics began, with the enrolment of the first patient. "Even without approved therapeutics, people are recovering from this disease, but of course, we could save many more lives with safe and effective therapeutics in our toolkit," the WHO head said. The current outbreak of Ebola in the DRC and Uganda began in May

A trial of potential treatments for the strain of virus behind the current deadly Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) has begun, the World Health Organization (WHO) has announced.

The first patient has been enrolled in the DRC, WHO chief Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus said on Thursday.

More than 1,400 cases and 438 deaths have been confirmed in the DRC alone, according to the WHO.

There are currently no approved vaccines or treatments for the Bundibugyo virus strain of the disease, which is highly infectious.

The current trial is sponsored by the WHO, and is being co-ordinated by scientists at the Institut National de Recherche Biomédicale in DRC, the Institute of Tropical Medicine in Belgium, and the University of Oxford in the UK.

Speaking to reporters from the WHO headquarters in Geneva on Thursday, Tedros said: "The clinical trial of two therapeutics began, with the enrolment of the first patient.

"Even without approved therapeutics, people are recovering from this disease, but of course, we could save many more lives with safe and effective therapeutics in our toolkit," the WHO head said.

Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus spoke to press on Thursday

The current outbreak of Ebola in the DRC and Uganda began in May, and has been declared a public health emergency by the WHO.

According to WHO data, there have been 1,406 confirmed cases in DRC, with 301 suspected cases and 438 deaths, as of 30 June.

There have also been 20 confirmed cases in Uganda, leading to two deaths, and one confirmed case in France, as of 1 July.

The disease is caused by a virus which attack's the body's immune systems and organs.

It normally infects animals, typically fruit bats, but outbreaks among humans can sometimes start when people handle infected animals.

People usually only become contagious after developing symptoms, and it takes two to 21 days for symptoms to appear.

They come on suddenly and start like flu or malaria with fever, headache and tiredness.

Vaccines must be developed for each individual species of Ebola, of which there are six, but only three are known to cause outbreaks.

[Lähde: STAT]
A clinical trial testing two drugs against the Bundibugyo ebolavirus, which is driving a fast-moving outbreak in Central Africa, is set to begin next week, World Health Organization officials said Wednesday.

The clinical trial — which will test both Gilead Sciences’ antiviral drug remdesivir and MappBio’s monoclonal antibody MBP-134 — will be conducted in the Democratic Republic of the Congo. The trial is designed to test whether either of the therapies is effective against this form of Ebola, and whether using the two in combination would be a more effective way to combat the disease.

payload.title: Ebolan lääkehoitokoe alkoi Kongon demokraattisessa tasavallassa
payload.summary: WHO:n mukaan Kongon demokraattisessa tasavallassa on aloitettu kliininen koe mahdollisista lääkehoidoista ebolan Bundibugyo-virusmuunnosta vastaan. Maassa on vahvistettu 1 406 tautitapausta ja 438 kuolemaa.
payload.content:
Maailman terveysjärjestö WHO kertoo, että Kongon demokraattisessa tasavallassa on aloitettu kliininen koe kahdesta mahdollisesta ebolan lääkehoidosta. Kokeen ensimmäinen potilas on otettu mukaan maassa, jossa Bundibugyo-virusmuunnoksen aiheuttama epidemia on johtanut satoihin kuolemiin ja jossa hyväksyttyjä hoitoja ei WHO:n mukaan vielä ole.

## Ensimmäinen potilas mukana kokeessa

WHO:n pääjohtaja Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus kertoi torstaina Genevessä, että kahden hoitomuodon kliininen koe on käynnistynyt ensimmäisen potilaan osallistumisella. Kyse on nykyisen epidemian taustalla olevasta Bundibugyo-virusmuunnoksesta, johon ei WHO:n mukaan ole tällä hetkellä hyväksyttyä rokotetta tai lääkehoitoa.

Tedrosin mukaan osa sairastuneista paranee myös ilman hyväksyttyjä hoitoja, mutta turvalliset ja tehokkaat lääkkeet voisivat pelastaa enemmän ihmishenkiä. Bundibugyo-muunnosta kuvataan erittäin tarttuvaksi, mikä korostaa hoitovaihtoehtojen kiireellisyyttä meneillään olevan epidemian aikana.

Kokeen rahoittajana toimii WHO. Sitä koordinoivat Kongon demokraattisen tasavallan Institut National de Recherche Biomédicale, Belgian Institute of Tropical Medicine ja Oxfordin yliopisto Britanniassa.

## Epidemia alkoi toukokuussa

Nykyinen ebolaepidemia Kongon demokraattisessa tasavallassa ja Ugandassa alkoi toukokuussa. WHO on julistanut tilanteen kansanterveydelliseksi hätätilanteeksi.

WHO:n tietojen mukaan Kongon demokraattisessa tasavallassa oli 30. kesäkuuta mennessä vahvistettu 1 406 ebolatapausta. Lisäksi epäiltyjä tapauksia oli 301 ja kuolemia 438. Luvut koskevat vain Kongon demokraattista tasavaltaa, jossa epidemian vaikutukset ovat olleet lähdeaineiston mukaan suurimmat.

Ugandassa oli 1. heinäkuuta mennessä vahvistettu 20 tartuntaa ja kaksi kuolemaa. Ranskassa oli vahvistettu yksi tapaus.

## Hoitojen tehoa arvioidaan kokeessa

Kliinisen kokeen käynnistyminen ei vielä tarkoita, että lääkkeet olisi todettu toimiviksi. WHO:n kertomien tietojen perusteella kyse on mahdollisten hoitojen tutkimisesta tilanteessa, jossa juuri Bundibugyo-virusmuunnosta vastaan ei ole hyväksyttyjä rokotteita tai lääkehoitoja.
